h1: The 4 Best 4-Slice Toaster Ovens of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 4 best 4-slice toaster ovens for 2026, from air fry models to compact budget picks, with specs and who each suits.
summary: The BLACK+DECKER 4-slice air fry toaster oven is the best 4-slice oven, the only pick here that adds air frying to a small body for $50 to $100. The BLACK+DECKER natural convection model suits bakers, and the Elite Gourmet ETO490 is the budget entry. The ETO449X is the most compact.
intro: The slice rating on a toaster oven is a marketing unit, not a measurement. Four slices of bread side by side fit very differently from four slices stacked in two rows, and a 9L cavity behaves nothing like a 12 inch pizza oven. Before you compare modes, settle what will actually go inside, because that decides whether a small oven earns counter space.

We ranked four models on cooking modes (air fry, convection, pizza), stated capacity, power and the price bucket each sits in. Everything comes from listing specs and owner reports, so treat wattage and capacity as a starting point and check the dimensions against your own counter and the dish you plan to use. Only the BLACK+DECKER pair adds a cooking mode beyond basic heat.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 4-Slice Air Fry Toaster Oven
products.verdict: The only pick here that adds air frying to a 4-slice body.
products.description:
This BLACK+DECKER pairs a 4-slice cavity with an air fry mode, which is rare in the $50 to $100 range. Air frying blows hot air hard across the food, so wings, fries and frozen snacks crisp instead of merely warming through. It lets one appliance replace both a toaster and a small air fryer on a crowded counter.

It ranks above the natural convection BLACK+DECKER because forced air crisps harder than gentle convection does. Against the Elite Gourmet ETOs below, it costs more but adds the mode people actually shop for.

Buy it if you want a single compact appliance for toast, reheating and crisping. The caveat is batch size: a small cavity means you cook in rounds. Skip it if you only toast bread, since you pay for a mode you will not use.
products.idealFor: Small kitchens that want toasting and crisping in one appliance.
products.skipIf: You only make toast and never fry.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 4-Slice Toaster Oven with Natural Convection
products.verdict: A convection 4-slice oven for buyers who skip the air fry premium.
products.description:
This model keeps the 4-slice footprint and adds natural convection for more even baking than a plain radiant oven. It sells in the same $50 to $100 range as the air fry version. Convection moves heat around the cavity, so the top and bottom of a tray finish together instead of one side browning first.

It lands second because it lacks a true air fry mode. If crisp results matter, the pick above handles that better. If you mostly bake, broil and toast, this one gives up little, and it saves you from paying for a feature you do not need. Against the ETO490, it adds convection for a higher price.

It suits households that want even heat for toast and small bakes without extra settings. The caveat is no fried-style results. Skip it if crispy food is the reason you are shopping.
cons: Same price as air fry model
products.idealFor: Bakers and toast eaters who want even heat without extras.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ETO490 9L/4-Slice Oven
products.verdict: A 9L cavity at the $25-50 bucket for light daily use.
products.description:
The ETO490 offers a 9L, 4-slice interior in the $25 to $50 range, roughly half the cost of the BLACK+DECKER models. That makes it the sensible entry for dorms and first apartments. Its basic heating is enough for toast, bagels and leftovers, and a low price lowers the pain if a student kitchen treats it roughly.

It ranks below the BLACK+DECKER pair because the listing shows no convection or air fry mode, so cooking is plain radiant heat. You trade features for price. Compared with the ETO449X, it lists a slightly bigger 9L cavity but no wattage and no pizza setting.

Buy it for toast, bagels and reheating. The caveat is the basic feature set, so if you want even baking or crisping, step up a price tier. Skip it if you need convection or air fry.
products.idealFor: Dorms and first apartments on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You need convection or air fry.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ETO449X Toaster Oven
products.verdict: The smallest footprint here, with a pizza function on top.
products.description:
The ETO449X is an 800W oven of roughly 9L with a pizza function, sitting in the $25 to $50 range. It is the most compact of the four. Wattage tells you how fast the element recovers after you open the door, and 800W suits toast and small reheats rather than a loaded tray.

It ranks last because 800W is modest and the cavity is the tightest, so four slices will be a snug fit and heat-up will lag stronger models. Its edge over the ETO490 is the pizza setting, which tunes heating for frozen pies. Against the BLACK+DECKER models, it lacks any convection or air fry mode.

It works for a small counter or a single person. The caveat is the modest power and snug interior. Anyone cooking for a family should pick a larger oven.
products.idealFor: Single users with very limited counter space.
products.skipIf: You cook for three or more people.

whatMatters.detail: A 4-slice label describes how much bread fits, not the real interior. Liter volume gives a better sense: 9L is tight for anything beyond toast. Check the interior dimensions on the listing, and measure the dish you would use, because a standard baking dish may not fit a cavity this size.

Air fry blows hot air quickly across food for a crisp finish, while natural convection gives gentler, more even heat. Air fry matters if you cook frozen fries or wings. Look for the mode named in the title or bullet points, as on the BLACK+DECKER pair, and ignore vague words like turbo. Check the rack height too, since fries need space to circulate.

Wattage governs how fast the oven heats and recovers after you open the door. Low-power models like the 800W ETO449X run slower on larger loads. Check the watt figure on the spec sheet before you buy, and remember that a missing figure, as on the ETO490 and BLACK+DECKER, tells you less, so ask the seller for the figure before you buy.

Toaster ovens throw heat out of the back and sides, so you need clearance, plus space above for a hinged door. Tight counters under cabinets can be a problem. Read the exterior dimensions and leave a few inches free. Heat damage to cabinets above is a common, avoidable mistake, and a heat-proof mat protects the counter.

Crumbs and grease build up on the bottom, which affects smell and fire risk. A pull-out crumb tray makes upkeep quick. Look for crumb tray mentions in the feature list. Air fry food drips more fat than toast, so a model you will clean weekly needs easy access to the tray and walls.

faq.q: Does a 4-slice toaster oven fit a pizza?
faq.a: Usually only small personal pizzas. The ETO449X lists a pizza function, but check the listed interior size against your pizza. A 9L cavity is not built for a 12 inch pie, and a frozen one may need to be cut or folded.

faq.q: Is air fry worth it in a toaster oven?
faq.a: It is if you cook frozen or fried-style foods often. If you only toast bread and bake, natural convection on the other BLACK+DECKER is enough, and cheaper models like the ETO490 cover basic toast and reheating.

faq.q: What is the common buying mistake?
faq.a: Assuming 4-slice means a large cavity. Liter volume is a better guide to what actually fits, as the ETO490 lists 9L and the ETO449X roughly 9L. A 4-slice label says little by itself.

faq.q: Can I put it under a cabinet?
faq.a: Leave clearance above and behind it. Heat vents out the back and top, so a tight spot under a cabinet can be a hazard. Pull it forward before use on small counters, and never cover the vents.

Unplug it, let it cool, and empty crumbs from the tray or bottom regularly. Wipe the interior with a damp cloth, and wash the rack, since baked-on grease smokes the next time you heat it. The air fry BLACK+DECKER needs grease wiped promptly.

faq.q: Is it better than a regular toaster?
faq.a: It is more versatile, since it bakes and reheats too. A basic toaster is faster and simpler for toast alone, and takes less counter space than any of these ovens. If you never bake, it is the cheaper choice.

finalTake: Buy the BLACK+DECKER air fry model if you want toast, reheating and crisping in one box. Take the convection version if you mostly bake and toast, and the ETO490 for a dorm or first apartment. The ETO449X suits one person with a tiny counter. Decide what you cook before you choose a mode, and measure the dish first.
